question: If the volume of a cuboid is 3x² - 27, then its possible dimensions are:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factorize the **volume expression** directly to find the dimensions.

Volume = 3x² − 27

Take common factor 3: 3(x² − 9)

Apply identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b): 3(x − 3)(x + 3)

**∴ The correct answer is 3, x − 3, x + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5238726c1f327de95fdfd6e2919a1ea6f2902e30eaf91dbddeb4e3b051a93adb.png] 

**Given:** Volume of cuboid = 3x² − 27

**Formula Used:** Volume of cuboid = **Length × Breadth × Height**

⇒ Volume = 3x² − 27

⇒ Volume = 3(x² − 9)

⇒ Volume = 3(x² − 3²)

⇒ Using identity **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**

⇒ Volume = 3 × (x − 3) × (x + 3)

⇒ Possible dimensions are 3, (x − 3), and (x + 3).

**∴ The correct answer is 3, x − 3, x + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Difference of squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is frequently used for factorizing volume expressions.

Volume of Cuboid

The volume of a cuboid is the product of its three dimensions: length (l), breadth (b), and height (h). V = l × b × h.

Factorization Method

To find dimensions from a polynomial volume, factorize the polynomial into three linear or constant factors.</p
